ai.fr: Lude & les métamorphoses célèbrent la sortie de leur premier EP MASCARADES à La Tricoterie. Découvrez des compositions dream-pop-électro explorant l'identité trans, la résilience et les contes d'enfance.
ai.nl: Lude & les métamorphoses vieren de release van hun debuut-ep MASCARADES in La Tricoterie. Ontdek dream-pop-electrocomposities over transidentiteit, veerkracht en sprookjes.

events.description: Lude & les métamorphoses is a musical project featuring the dream-pop-electro compositions of Lude Vial, Zach Ruegg, and Valentin Perroud (Pylone). The group, which performs live as a trio with Pierre Ferrand (drums, bass, and vocals/keyboards), explores personal and intimate themes related to trans identity, disillusionment, dreams, and resilience, using various images and symbols. The musical performance also draws on the world of childhood, various fairy tales, and pop culture references to reimagine their relevance today. Through a poetic and surrealistic universe, Lude & les métamorphoses seek to create new spaces to shed light on certain experiences and emotions through music. At their release party at La Tricoterie in Brussels on November 27, 2026, they will unveil their debut EP, *MASCARADES*, conceived as a short 8-track album, mixed by Shinji Hashimoto and mastered by Remy Lebbos (Rare Sound Studio).

summary.fr: Dans le paisible village de Fourbichet-les-Trois-Collines, Didier Masseur est retrouvé assassiné sur le clavier de son orgue.

ai.en: Le Petit Chapeau Rond Rouge hosts Ronald Alexandre in Meurtre au village. Step into Fourbichet-les-Trois-Collines for a colorful, biting solo show where the audience helps solve a sordid mystery.
ai.fr: Le Petit Chapeau Rond Rouge accueille Ronald Alexandre pour Meurtre au village. Plongez dans un seul en scène mordant où le public aide à dénouer une sordide histoire.
ai.nl: Le Petit Chapeau Rond Rouge brengt Meurtre au village met Ronald Alexandre. Duik in een bijtende monoloog waarin het publiek helpt om een duistere moord op te lossen.

events.description: Les langues se délient, les vieilles rancœurs refont surface, les secrets n'en sont plus et l'accord joué par le poids du corps de Didier est affreux. À travers une galerie de personnages hauts en couleur, comme il est convenu de dire dans toute bonne présentation de specactle, de spetcle, de spectacle, Ronald Alexandre nous dresse le portrait du village et de ses habitants dans un seul en scène haut en couleur ! Mince, j'ai déjà dit, haut en couleur. Virevoltant, alors. Non seulement le public découvre une histoire sensible et mordante, mais en plus, il devient lui-même partie prenante du dénouement de cette sordide histoire... Bienvenue à Fourbichet-les-Trois-Collines !

title.en: LA KAMIKAZÉ : Et une bourrasque éventra le silence
title.fr: LA KAMIKAZÉ : Et une bourrasque éventra le silence
title.nl: LA KAMIKAZÉ : Et une bourrasque éventra le silence

summary.fr: Avec le théâtre, rendre visible l’inceste : un problème de société. En Belgique, 9% de la population a été victime d’inceste, soit 1 personne sur 10. Dans ce contexte, La Villa a accueillie en résidence et accompagné Aline La Sardine pour…

events.description: L’inceste est encore entouré de silences, de tabous et de mécanismes qui rendent sa dénonciation particulièrement difficile. Le théâtre permet de mettre en mots et en regard une réalité, pour ouvrir un espace de réflexion et d’actions collectives. La Kamikazé Et une bourrasque éventra le silence À 5 ans,une petite fille s’est envolée, comme une oie bernache nonnette. Adulte, elle recompose, mots après mots, les morceaux éclatés de sa mémoire amnésique . Elle se cogne dans le labyrinthe de son cerveau foudroyé. Tétanie. Chute. Silence. Alors les sensations reviennent, le corps se débat, les souvenirs de l’enfance remontent à la surface. Viol(ence)s, mensonges des adultes, dérives judiciaires, addictions … survie. La Kamikazé ouvre les portes de l’horreur. Elle empoigne la honte, le doute, la peur. Elle lance sa rage et sort du silence. Ce seule en scène est combat contre la mort où la vulnérabilité est assumée. La Kamikazé appelle à voler ensemble, une nuées d’oies bernaches, contre la culture de l’inceste. events.description: Jazztutta is a dynamic ensemble led by Belgian-Italian saxophonist, pianist, and composer Assunta Di Pasquale. Blending jazz, gospel, and samba, the group delivers a vibrant repertoire of both standards and original compositions.This musical project stands out through the versatility of its leader, who seamlessly transitions from alto saxophone to keyboards and vocals. She is backed by a lineup of seasoned musicians: Paolo Loveri on guitar, Benoît Vanderstraeten on bass, and Bruno Castellucci on drums.For this concert, Jazztutta will present its new album, recently recorded in Rio de Janeiro with remarkable musicians, including Marcelo Martins, Rafael Rocha, Danilo Sinna, Felipe Alves, and Dedy Coutinho.For this special evening, the quartet will have the pleasure of welcoming Vincent Mardens on tenor saxophone, thus forming the Jazztutta 5tet.

events.description: The only one of its kind, « the Brussels guitar fiesta » attracts a large crowd and over the years has established itself as one of the major festivals in Europe. The splendid Hay Doun Cultural Center and the Conservatoire Royal de Bruxelles will host concerts, master classes, a lecture, an exhibition as well as the public final rounds of the national competition, the international competition and the composition competition. Classical, jazzy, Spanish, Latin American, modern music… The many facets of the world's most played instrument will be showcased thanks to a rich and varied programme : solo guitar, duo, ensemble, guitar with orchestra, accordion, violin, flute, percussion… Always seeking new experiences, the festival offers the public the chance to attend several Belgian premieres and listen to big names in guitar music from various countries (Belgium, Spain, France, Germany, Czech Republic, Austria, China…) as well as young artists on the verge of a promising career, for whom the festival serves as a launch pad. The 2026 selection, via a new exhibition, pays tribute to the Masters Ilse & Nicolas Alfonso, who opened the first guitar classes in the Belgian Music Academies as well as the guitar class at the Conservatoire Royal de Bruxelles in 1965, thereby becoming the founders of the Belgian Guitar School. The festival is also dedicating one evening to Jean Baily (1937-2026), Composer, Honorary Director of the Conservatoire royal de Bruxelles and founder of its Jazz…

ai.nl: Winterpret viert haar 25ste verjaardag op iconische plekken in Brussel. Ontdek de kerstmarkt, de lichtshow op de Grote Markt en een speciaal Baskisch dorp.

events.description: From 27 November 2026 to 3 January 2027, Brussels celebrates the 25th anniversary of Winter Wonders. For a quarter of a century, this much-loved event has brought locals and visitors of all ages together to experience the magic of the festive season, in a warm and welcoming atmosphere that blends tradition, conviviality and creativity. At the heart of the city, the Christmas market and its many chalets invite visitors to discover delicious local specialities, handcrafted creations and gift ideas. From Place de la Monnaie to Place Royale, Grand-Place, Place Sainte-Catherine, Vismet, Place de la Bourse, Place De Brouckère, the Black Tower, Place de la Madeleine and, finally, Place Poelaert, Winter Wonders brings its festive atmosphere to iconic locations throughout Brussels. A magnificent Christmas tree and a spectacular sound and light show illuminate Grand-Place, while attractions for all ages, cultural activities and artistic creations add to the experience. This anniversary edition also shines a spotlight on Béarn, the Pyrenees and the Basque Country, with a dedicated village at Place de la Bourse, inviting visitors to discover the region’s traditions and culture. events.description: Commissioned by Kanal, Otobong Nkanga transforms one of the vast open spaces into an intimate site for encounter and co-creation. At the heart of the installation are wooden looms where participants, who have received prior training, work side by side. Skills and experiences are exchanged. Threads are woven, and personal and collective stories become interlaced. Weaving turns into a "social act", a joint endeavour that contributes to the evolving artwork. In the setting of the new museum – formerly a car garage and large-scale production site – the installation invites you to reflect on the labour and the economic structures that underpin cultural institutions and the world at large. In her work, Otobong Nkanga examines how these systems and processes shape relationships between people, materials and spaces. By redistributing work and resources across a network of partners and participants, the social responsibilities of the museum and its commitments to community-building, sustainability and shared authorship are highlighted. Otobong Nkanga lives and works in Antwerp and is recognised as one of the most influential artists working today. She received a Special Mention at the 58th Venice Biennale and she was commissioned by MoMA in New York in 2024 to create a work for their Atrium. Among her many accolades are the Yanghyun Prize, the Belgian Art Prize and the Nasher Art Prize.

events.description: With right?, Banu Cennetoğlu presents the articles of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) in bouquets of gold letter balloons in Kanal’s showroom. Each bundle represents one of the 30 articles of the Declaration. Proclaimed by the General Assembly of the United Nations in Paris on 10 December 1948, three years after the end of the Second World War, the UDHR sets out, for the first time, the fundamental human rights to be universally protected. Translated into over 500 languages, it is one of the most widely circulated documents in existence. But what do these rights really mean in a world where they are still and persistently violated? For Kanal’s opening, the artist – who lives and works in Istanbul – presents all 30 articles together for the very first time. Brussels is a fitting place for this gathering: it is home to the European institutions and NATO headquarters, organisations that claim to protect peace and democracy. As the days pass, the balloons deflate and lose their sheen. The letters progressively deform and potentially transform. This gradual collapse exposes the vulnerability of human rights: they exist only as long as they are actively upheld, defended and reimagined. right? is both a testament and a warning – a reminder that human rights are never permanently secured. Banu Cennetoğlu’s work investigates how narratives, data and documents circulate in public space and how they shape collective understanding.

Rooted in the ancient connection between breathing and rhythm, RESPIRIA! approaches sound-making as a shared and accessible act. The national anthem is no longer a closed composition but an open, collective experience. This commission forms part of How to open, the first year of Protocols for opening the museum, a three-year inquiry into what it means for a new museum in Brussels to be truly open, welcoming and public.

events.description: BILDYin builds on Bildy, the long-running neighbourhood project by artist Einat Tuchman that originated in Molenbeek. It embodies what the world needs more of: connection, dialogue and collective imagination. Step into an immersive environment featuring an exhibition of practices, where archive and visual material come together with the creative process of local artists and craftspeople. If you'd like to get involved yourself, join an exchange dinner, take a dance class, take part in a performance or lend a hand in the collective soup kitchen. Perhaps you'll even sign up for a creative youth programme or join a discussion on pressing social issues. BILDYin concludes with Urban Ritual, a participatory performance in Kanal's public spaces, in which movement, music and shared presence combine to create a temporary space of connection. The BILDY community blurs the boundaries between audience and performers and invites everyone to join in through simple gestures and actions, bringing the streets of Kanal to life together.

events.description: This programme brings together documentaries, artist films, archival footage and television reports tracing the creation and opening of large-scale institutions, including the Centre Georges Pompidou in Paris in 1977, S.M.A.K. in Ghent in 1999 and Tate Modern in London in 2000. Across three thematic loops, the programme follows museums from conception and construction to public inauguration. Shown over the weeks surrounding Kanal's opening, the films consider how art institutions introduce themselves through narratives of change, possibility and promise – and how artists have at times responded to them. This programme forms part of How to open, the first year of Protocols for opening the museum, a three-year inquiry into what it means for a new museum in Brussels to be truly open, welcoming and public.

summary.fr: Dans sa nouvelle performance CRI CRI CLAP ROARRRR, Sharon Hayes explore les défis et les contradictions liés à la prise de parole en public aujourd’hui.

ai.en: Sharon Hayes brings a megaphone chorus to Kanal - Centre Pompidou's public spaces. Performers explore queer action, community building, and public presence as part of the museum's opening inquiry.
ai.fr: Sharon Hayes investit les espaces publics du Kanal - Centre Pompidou avec un chœur de porte-voix. Des performeurs explorent l'action queer et la construction communautaire pour l'ouverture du musée.

events.description: A group of performers uses megaphones to amplify, direct and misdirect speech through Kanal's public spaces, exploring what forms of presence, solidarity and political imagination can emerge in this moment of crisis. Their voices shift between legible language and energetic force, forming a bullhorn chorus whose sonic field creates conditions for call and response. Here, the megaphone becomes a tool for assembling a community whose members can speak with and alongside one another. Drawing on transnational genealogies of queer action, CRI CRI CLAP ROARRRR remains invested in the unknown futures of queer life. Hayes considers what it means for a public institution to emerge in present-day Brussels and how its arrival might reshape the city. What forms of orientation, movement and sociality must be imagined and negotiated as a new cultural institution opens its doors to the public? In times of violence and erasure, how might people act with love, hope, rage and vision to create new fields of possibility? This commission forms part of How to open, the first year of Protocols for opening the museum, a three-year inquiry into what it means for a new museum in Brussels to be truly open, welcoming and public.

ai.en: NO SHOW at Kanal - Centre Pompidou features twenty Brussels artists exploring the museum's duty to entertain. Wander through a five-room immersive experience by Deborah Bowmann and Maoupa Mazzocchetti.
ai.fr: NO SHOW au Kanal - Centre Pompidou rassemble vingt artistes bruxellois autour de la question du divertissement dans les musées. Explorez cette expérience immersive signée Deborah Bowmann et Maoupa Mazzocchetti.
ai.nl: NO SHOW in Kanal - Centre Pompidou brengt twintig Brusselse kunstenaars samen die de amusementsdrang van musea bevragen. Ontdek deze vijf kamers tellende installatie van Deborah Bowmann en Maoupa Mazzocchetti.

events.description: Can a museum entertain? On the site of Brussels’ first luna park, artist duo Deborah Bowmann, musician Maoupa Mazzocchetti and twenty Brussels artists ask this question with a hint of irony. Their provisional answer is NO SHOW, a group exhibition in which art, light, sound and live performance come together in a fully immersive experience across five rooms. Visitors move between front and backstage, fact and fabrication – humour functioning as both lure and critique. Much like Deborah Bowmann's former artist-run space in the Brussels borough of Saint-Gilles – which continually reinvented itself, from a shoe shop to a parking lot to their own living quarters – this exhibition also refuses easy definition. The twenty artists inhabit Deborah Bowmann’s scenography and Mazzocchetti’s soundscape. In a time where art has to vie for attention amid relentless spectacle, the artists confront the expectation to entertain. They both embrace and reject the consumption of their identities, works and narratives. Using humour and seriousness in equal measure, NO SHOW explores how an exhibition might perform itself, subtly unsettling the boundaries and expectations of the museum. With NO SHOW, Deborah Bowmann – the alias of artist duo Amaury Daurel and Victor Delestre – and Mazzocchetti embark on their largest project to date. It brings some of their mutable energy to Kanal, while highlighting how support, community and solidarity have long been pivotal in shaping the Brussels’ art scene…

summary.fr: Au milieu de lʹagitation du nouveau musée et de la ville, lʹinstallation sonore Blindsight de Manon de Boer nous invite à ralentir. En collaboration avec la chorégraphe Latifa Laâbissi et le concepteur sonore Laszlo Umbreit, de Boer fait…
summary.nl: Te midden van de drukte in het nieuwe museum en de stad nodigt de geluidsinstallatie Blindsight van Manon de Boer uit om te vertragen. Samen met choreograaf Latifa Laâbissi en geluidsontwerper Laszlo Umbreit brengt de Boer stemmen tot…

ai.en: Blindsight by Manon de Boer at Kanal - Centre Pompidou invites you to slow down. Experience a sensory sound installation where hidden speakers let you feel the narrative.
ai.fr: Blindsight de Manon de Boer au Kanal - Centre Pompidou vous invite au ralentissement. Vivez une installation sonore sensorielle où des haut-parleurs cachés font ressentir le récit.
ai.nl: Blindsight van Manon de Boer in Kanal - Centre Pompidou nodigt uit tot vertraging. Ervaar een zintuiglijke installatie waar verborgen luidsprekers het verhaal voelbaar maken.

events.description: Amidst the bustle of the new museum, Blindsight invites you to slow down. Take a seat in a cinema chair and dive into the soundtrack of a film you can feel rather than see. This installation by artist Manon de Boer, collaborating with choreographer Latifa Laâbissi and sound designer Laszlo Umbreit, is the final part of a trilogy that began with the performance Ghost Party 1 (2022) and the film Ghost Party 2 (2022). In that film, de Boer and Laâbissi lend their voices to artists and writers who inspired them, from Chantal Akerman and Beyoncé to Anne Carson and Marguerite Duras. The dialogues and soundscapes were later translated into a sound installation, now reimagined for Kanal. Blindsight immerses you in a carefully composed sensory environment. Sound emanates from speakers concealed inside vases – a nod to the vases featured in Ghost Party 2 – which are dispersed throughout the space. Each vase corresponds to one of the "ghosts" to whom the artists give their voices. Here, the ear takes precedence over the eye. In a world saturated with stimuli, the installation creates an interval of stillness, a near-meditative space in which the whispers of forgotten voices resurface. Manon de Boer is a central figure in the Belgian art scene, known for her video work that brings together music, dance and film. Through her filmed portraits, she explores the perception of time and space. This work is part of the Kanal collection.

summary.en: For several years, Joëlle Tuerlinckx kept a close eye on the construction of Kanal. With a light show and an explosive symphony of sounds co-created with Christoph Fink, she puts you under hypnosis and introduces you to the underground…
summary.fr: Pendant plusieurs années, Joëlle Tuerlinckx a suivi les travaux de construction du musée. Dans une mise en lumière et sous une symphonie explosive de sons qu’elle réalise en collaboration avec l’artiste Christoph Fink, elle mène les…
summary.nl: Gedurende meerdere jaren volgde Joëlle Tuerlinckx de bouw van Kanal van nabij. Met een lichtshow en een explosieve geluidssymfonie die ze samen met Christoph Fink creëert, brengt ze je onder hypnose en laat ze je kennismaken met zowel het…

ai.en: Joëlle Tuerlinckx presents an underground exhibition at Kanal - Centre Pompidou. Explore a cavernous space shaped by light, sound compositions, and building site memories.
ai.fr: Joëlle Tuerlinckx présente une exposition souterraine au Kanal - Centre Pompidou. Explorez un espace façonné par la lumière, des compositions sonores et des bruits de chantier.
ai.nl: Joëlle Tuerlinckx presenteert een underground tentoonstelling in Kanal - Centre Pompidou. Ontdek een ruimte gevormd door licht, geluidscomposities en werfherinneringen.

events.description: For the opening of Kanal, Joëlle Tuerlinckx personally picked an exhibition space: the most underground, deep in the foundations of the museum. For several years, she kept a close eye on the building works: the pumping of groundwater into the canal, the construction of the walls, the pounding of hammers on site. In this way, she saw the space unfold for "the first time". Now, she shares those first impressions with the public. Through "Light figures" that weave a universe of real and false time, and a sound composition co-created with artist Christoph Fink, she sends visitors through the room’s emptiness. Two different lighting systems reveal the cavernous space: one casts a conventional museum light, while the other is more theatrical and plays with atmosphere, time and rhythm. Sometimes they overlap unexpectedly – like a solar eclipse – creating a choreography that summons, often with humour, the past and possible future of the space. The silence is broken by announcements, alarms and other sounds: noises from the building site, or disorienting room descriptions and texts by Tuerlinckx, read by different voices in various languages. This polyphony transports visitors through the museum's underground and the invisible foundations of Tuerlinckx's art, as if under hypnosis. Meanwhile, the sound of water evokes the Brussels marshes, the proximity of the canal and the porous nature of this subterranean space. This sense of permeability also blurs the boundaries between inside…

ai.en: Joshua Serafin presents a film installation at Kanal - Centre Pompidou exploring ancestry and migration. Discover a personal journey bridging the Philippines and Belgium.
ai.fr: Joshua Serafin présente une installation filmée au Kanal - Centre Pompidou autour de la généalogie et de la migration. Découvrez un voyage entre les Philippines et la Belgique.
ai.nl: Joshua Serafin presenteert een filminstallatie in Kanal - Centre Pompidou over afkomst en migratie. Ontdek een persoonlijke reis die de Filipijnen en België verbindt.

events.description: In 1909, Joshua Serafin’s Japanese great-great-grandfather migrated to the Philippines. Commissioned by Kanal, the film installation Whispering pleas of the eternal echoes invites you to join the search for ancestry and belonging. Motivated by a desire for connection and knowledge of the past, Serafin brings together multiple characters and entities across regions and eras. Footage from the Philippines flows into scenes filmed in Belgium. In a universe of Serafin’s own making, past and present generations converse as if across a cosmic threshold. Joshua Serafin’s practice centres on choreography and queerness, exploring how body, space and audience co-produce meaning. Serafin’s personal journey – from Manila to Hong Kong and now Brussels – fuels their ongoing inquiry into how migration and displacement impact identity and resilience. In their performances, Serafin brings together alter egos and fictional characters within "speculative cosmologies". These spaces for imagination, liberation and transformation challenge systems that control and constrain bodies, as in the performance VOID, which was critically acclaimed at the 60th Venice Biennale in 2024.

summary.nl: Honderd jaar geleden ging het massaal geproduceerde beeld van een Mangbetu-vrouw viraal. An infinite woman verkent hoe het kenmerkende profiel van de Mangbetu uit Congo na Citroëns La Croisière Noire-expeditie uitgroeide tot een…

ai.en: An infinite woman at Kanal - Centre Pompidou explores colonial imagery and its subversion. The exhibition contrasts archival history with works by artists of African descent.
ai.fr: An infinite woman au Kanal - Centre Pompidou explore l'imagerie coloniale et sa subversion. L'exposition confronte l'histoire des archives et des œuvres d'artistes diasporiques.
ai.nl: An infinite woman in Kanal - Centre Pompidou onderzoekt koloniale beeldvorming en subversie. De tentoonstelling confronteert archieven met werk van kunstenaars van Afrikaanse afkomst.

events.description: In 1925, a Mangbetu woman from north-eastern Congo became the viral campaign image of La Croisière Noire, a colonial propaganda expedition across the African continent, sponsored by Citroën. In 1934, construction began on Citroën’s flagship garage in Brussels, marketing the idea of imperial conquest as much as cars. Converted into the museum Kanal, the building reopens with the exhibition An infinite woman, revisiting in two parts how the Mangbetu women functioned as a colonial symbol and how artists of African descent have reclaimed and subverted this imagery until the present day. The first act is an archival investigation that traces how Mangbetus went viral as an "ethnographic fetish" consumed in the West as a pre-internet meme, through magazines, exhibitions and films. The second act shows how artists from the African diaspora – such as Raphaël Barontini, Sonia Barrett, Roméo Mivekannin, Faith Ringgold, Barbara Walker and Carrie Mae Weems – break the algorithm, reappropriating images and archives that generate new forms of knowledge and visibility. The subtitle of the exhibition refers to cultural historian Saidiya Hartman’s essay Venus in Two Acts (2008). Inspired by this influential work about post-slavery society, it celebrates the limitless Black female imagination in resisting the toxicity of colonial imagery. Ultimately, An infinite woman is an exercise in defying gravity: recognising the full weight of the colonial past while refusing to let it continue defining…

summary.nl: Met een knipoog naar de Brusselse kunstenaar Marcel Broodthaers nodigt Clémentine Deliss je uit in het Département des Pièges. Je vindt er een reeks verrassende objecten en schilderijen uit 11 Brusselse musea en werken van hedendaagse…

ai.en: Département des Pièges at Kanal - Centre Pompidou brings together traps, decoys, and contemporary artworks. Explore visual illusions loaned from eleven Brussels museums.
ai.fr: Département des Pièges au Kanal - Centre Pompidou réunit pièges, leurres et œuvres contemporaines. Explorez des objets insolites prêtés par onze musées bruxellois.
ai.nl: Département des Pièges in Kanal - Centre Pompidou brengt vallen, lokmiddelen en hedendaagse kunst samen. Verken visuele illusies uit elf Brusselse musea.

events.description: With Département des Pièges, Clémentine Deliss invites you to closely study an unusual assembly of objects and paintings. These nets, snares, decoys and visual illusions all play on the concept of the trap or the lure. Rarely exhibited, they are loaned from the collections of 11 Brussels museums, from the Design Museum Brussels and AfricaMuseum to the National Museum of Resistance and the Museum of Medicine. The diverse pieces are displayed alongside works by contemporary artists such as Guillaume Bijl, Kasper Bosmans, Laurent Dupont, Aline Bouvy, Pélagie Gbaguidi, Valérie Mannaerts, Miao Miao and many others whose practice also reflects on the idea of the trap. The title pays tribute to the Département des Aigles, the fictional museum of Marcel Broodthaers, one of the leading surrealists and conceptual artists of the 1960s in Brussels and beyond. The mise-en-scène of the exhibition similarly invokes the merging of a museum and university into a "department" or faculty for visual thinking. At the centre of the room is a large table in the shape of a lung. Here, historical artefacts and contemporary works appear side by side, while paintings by Belgian and international artists from the 17th to the 21st century line the walls. An accompanying booklet provides additional information about the context of each exhibit and a special edition of the artists’ and writers’ publication Metronome presents further reading on traps and their metaphors. Take a seat in this Département des…

summary.fr: A truly immense journey vous guide à travers les forces qui ont mis les personnes, les idées et les formes artistiques en mouvement depuis le début du 20e siècle jusquʹà aujourdʹhui. Lʹexposition regroupe les icônes de lʹart moderne que…
summary.nl: A truly immense journey neemt je mee op een reis langs wat mensen, ideeën en kunst in beweging zet, van het begin van de 20e eeuw tot nu. Van moderne iconen als Lygia Clark, Sonia Delaunay, Alberto Giacometti, Natalia Goncharova, Wifredo…

ai.en: A truly immense journey at Kanal - Centre Pompidou gathers over 350 works exploring human movement. Drift through modern and contemporary art addressing migration and trade.
ai.fr: A truly immense journey au Kanal - Centre Pompidou rassemble plus de 350 œuvres sur la mobilité humaine. Parcourez l'art moderne et contemporain lié aux migrations.
ai.nl: A truly immense journey in Kanal - Centre Pompidou brengt ruim 350 werken samen over menselijke mobiliteit. Dwaal door moderne en hedendaagse kunst over migratie en handel.

events.description: A truly immense journey invites you on a voyage without a fixed destination – an exploration of the forces that propel people, ideas and artistic practices across geographies and histories, from the early 1900s to the present. More than 350 major works, predominantly from the Centre Pompidou and Kanal, but also from other Belgian public and private collections are gathered within the exhibition. Visitors are invited to drift between places and movements, encountering modern art icons such as Lygia Clark, Sonia Delaunay, Natalia Goncharova, Henri Matisse, Wifredo Lam, Katarzyna Kobro, Pablo Picasso and Alberto Giacometti, alongside contemporary international and Brussels-based artists including Sammy Baloji, Edith Dekyndt, Aglaia Konrad and Hana Miletić. The juxtaposition of historical and contemporary works creates unexpected constellations that shed new light on pertinent debates in relation to the city of Brussels and art histories. Inspired by the museum’s location along the Charleroi-Brussels canal – a historical conduit of trade, exchange and migration – A truly immense journey unfolds in three movements. The first examines stories of circulation, tracing how people around the world, including in Belgium, are displaced for political, social or environmental reasons. Another floor situates early 20th-century European Modernism within its colonial entanglements with Africa, Oceania and the Caribbean, and highlights the role of travelling and migrating artists in…

events.description: Plongez au cœur de l’un des quartiers les plus vivants et iconoclastes de Bruxelles. Ce parcours immersif vous invite à découvrir l'histoire fascinante d'un quartier où se croisent créativité, rébellion et engagement social. La genèse de quelques grands mouvements artistiques Des personnages et des personnalités inspirantes Découvrez les lieux de vie de quelques penseurs rebelles de leurs époques : Karl Marx, Proudhon, Victor Serge, Neel Doff,... L'éphémère "Université Nouvelle", version radicale de l'ULB La maison de naissance d'Audrey Hepburn Des nombreuses histoires et anecdotes inattendues Laissez-vous guider à travers les rues pittoresques d'Ixelles, où l’art se mêle à l’histoire et où les traces du passé se retrouvent sur chaque coin de rue. De l’effervescence des ateliers d'artistes aux traces laissées par les mouvements anarchistes et les luttes sociales, chaque étape de cette visite vous fera découvrir une facette unique de la ville, entre héritage et modernité. Vous explorerez les galeries d'art cachées et découvrirez des lieux emblématiques qui ont été des refuges pour les artistes et des points de ralliement pour les militants. Notre guide passionné vous racontera les anecdotes inédites qui ont forgé l’identité rebelle et artistique d'Ixelles, tout en vous révélant des lieux secrets, souvent ignorés des ixellois eux-mêmes. Que vous soyez amateur d'art, curieux d'histoire ou passionné par les luttes sociales, cette visite vous offrira un regard original et profond…

ai.en: At Kanal - Centre Pompidou, Apparatus 22 presents A museum lover has questions. This installation invites visitors to reflect on the role and meaning of a new museum.
ai.fr: À Kanal - Centre Pompidou, Apparatus 22 présente A museum lover has questions. Cette installation invite le public à réfléchir sur le rôle et le sens d'un nouveau musée.
ai.nl: Apparatus 22 presenteert in Kanal - Centre Pompidou A museum lover has questions. Deze installatie nodigt uit tot reflectie over de rol en betekenis van een nieuw museum.

events.description: For Kanal's opening, the artist collective Apparatus 22 presents A museum lover has questions, a new chapter in their ongoing series of confetti explosions. Ten questions probe the possibilities and pitfalls of a new institution. Over a period of three years, interventions and instructions will gradually infiltrate Kanal, inviting people who are fascinated by museums to reflect on their role and meaning. Blending fiction, storytelling and critique, the work keeps questions alive rather than seeking definitive answers or consensus, treating the act of asking as fundamental to public institutions. This commission forms part of How to open, the first year of Protocols for opening the museum, a three-year inquiry into what it means for a new museum in Brussels to be truly open, welcoming and public.

events.description: On 28 and 29 November 2026, the Ostend and Brussels based music label STROOM takes over Botanique for a two-day festival bringing together more than 45 artists from Belgium and abroad. STROOM began in 2013 as stroom.tv, an experimental and idiosyncratic audiovisual online radio station founded by Ziggy Devriendt (DJ Nosedrip) and friends. What started as a small, open-ended platform eventually grew into a record label in 2016, one that has kept moving, shifting and expanding while staying guided by a simple curiosity: what happens when music refuses to sit neatly in a category? Over the past ten years, STROOM has released more than 130 records, spanning ambient, folk, pop, electronic music, improvisation, contemporary composition and obscure archival discoveries. Its catalogue includes music by Pablo’s Eye, Voice Actor, Felicity J Lord, Milan W., Merope, Jan Van Den Broeke, Sofie Birch and Enno Velthuys, alongside a growing network of new voices and international collaborations. From its beginnings in Ostend to its current base in Brussels, STROOM has developed into a distinctive presence within the international experimental music scene, less concerned with defining a genre than with following a particular way of listening. For its tenth anniversary, Botanique becomes a meeting point for this sprawling STROOM universe. Artists from across the label’s catalogue will share the stage with more recent additions, while solo performances sit alongside unusual collaborations and…

events.description: Affichant sa large façade en pierre blanche, l’hôtel Winssinger fut conçu entre 1894 et 1897 par Victor Horta dans un « esprit d’art total » cher au maître de l’Art nouveau. L’architecte y intègre une ample cage d'escalier baignée de lumière et un jardin d'hiver rehaussé d’une sublime verrière. Le passage du temps et les occupants successifs ayant dénaturé l’œuvre initiale, le propriétaire actuel, passionné par l'œuvre de Victor Horta, a mené plusieurs campagnes de restauration afin de lui rendre son lustre d'antan et restituer moult détails de décor. Un travail de longue haleine semé d'embuches ! Ainsi la visite offre-t-elle de retrouver l’état initial de l'immeuble habillé de courbes organiques, de notes florales, de vitraux décoratifs, de sols en mosaïques, de matériaux précieux ainsi que les incontournables structures apparentes en acier, autant d’éléments qui signent le travail de l’architecte. Vous serez aussi surpris de découvrir une magnifique galerie moderniste, œuvre de l'architecte Henri Aimé Jacobs, à l'arrière du bâtiment.

events.description: Founded in 2016 on the initiative of multidisciplinary artist William Kentridge and theatre director Bronwyn Lace, The Centre for the Less Good Idea is an experimental platform for live arts based in Johannesburg. Conceived as a space for creation through collective experimentation and improvisation, the Centre brings together music, poetry, moving image, visual arts and mediation, and gathers artists from a wide range of backgrounds. In 2024, musician and composer Neo Muyanga became the Centre's impresario and developed a programme of regular activities there.This season, marked by the imprint of Grand Invité William Kentridge, offers Bozar audiences an exceptional opportunity to discover the work and the artists that make The Centre for the Less Good Idea one of the most inspiring creative spaces in the world. Two performances presented on the same evening will bear witness to this: A Defence of the Less Good Idea, a lecture-performance by William Kentridge, and Sounding Pictures, a screening of a silent film specially created for Bozar and accompanied live by musicians and performers closely associated with the Centre. A Defence of the Less Good Idea Lecture-performance Duration: 45 minutes Sounding Pictures Film and live music Duration: 1 hour William Kentridge, lead performer Bronwyn Lace, director of The Defence Neo Muyanga, musical director for Sounding Pictures Anathi Conjwa, vocals, composition Vusi Mdoyi, vocals, dance, percussion Shane Cooper, double bass Angelo…

events.description: D’un mot à l’autre, Koua et Hétoi jouent avec ceux-ci et juste parce qu’elles l’ont dit, deviennent Mouche, Ibis, Lapin, Vache, Eléphant-fourmi, jusqu’à faire pipi ici mais c’est interdit… Ce court texte théâtral de l’auteur-illustrateur Claude Ponti, riche en rebondissements fantaisistes, invente tout un monde où chaque animal convoqué est une surprise. Quand la langue se débride, c’est tout l’imaginaire qui s’évade. On s’y perd, on est ici ou là, on est là-bas ou ici. On y chante aussi, au clair de lune. Et au loin, on s’interroge : est-ce qu’on comprend ce qu’on entend ? Est-ce qu’on entend ce qu’on comprend ? Un spectacle jubilatoire qui dit beaucoup, sans en avoir l’air.

events.description: He spans a century... or rather two! The composer György Kurtág is one of the most remarkable figures in contemporary music creation of the 20th and 21st centuries. Moreover, last February he reached the – equally remarkable – age of 100. While building upon the legacy of his Hungarian compatriot Béla Bartók, who preceded him by a generation, he was also inspired by his deep connection with Robert Schumann and Johann Sebastian Bach (whose scores he sometimes arranges). Kurtág is known for his countless, often very short compositions, in which he devotes the utmost care to every note. To celebrate the birthday of this exceptional artist, Ars Musica and the Hungarian Cultural Institute are organizing a three-part Kurtág Day. The program starts with children who participated in Laurence Mekhitarian's workshops. They will play pieces from Játékok (Playing): piano pieces that allow them to discover the keyboard through play. Next, it is the turn of more experienced musicians. The evening concludes with an ensemble of clarinet, violin, piano, and the fascinating cimbalom (a well-known Hungarian string instrument, beloved by street musicians, whose horizontally stretched strings are struck with small hammers). A wonderful opportunity to bring together all of Kurtág's musical influences, from Bach to today. A concert for young and old... from 1 to 101 years old? Játékok 16.00-17.00 Concert by students of the Brussels academies 18.00-19.00 The Centuries of Kurtág 20.00-21.15

Petit à petit se construit un monde enchanté, fait de fontaines, de bassines et de robinets. Un voyage musical et lumineux qui éveille les sens des tout-petits, reflète la douce sensation des premiers bains, tout en rappelant la préciosité de cette ressource.

events.description: Brussels By Foot vous a concocté un parcours inédit au détour d’une dizaine de stations pour vous faire découvrir quelques-unes des oeuvres les plus emblématiques du métro bruxellois. Une balade conviviale, originale et inédite loin du métro-boulot-dodo ! Le parcours est pensé pour vous montrer la plus grande variété d’œuvres, que ce soit au niveau stylistique, de matériaux et techniques utilisés ou de thématiques abordées… QU’ALLEZ-VOUS DÉCOUVRIR ? Avez-vous déjà prêté attention aux œuvres dans le métro ? Pourquoi telle gravure à tel endroit ? Pourquoi cette fresque se trouve ici, et cette peinture là-bas ? Quels sont leurs liens avec cette station particulière, avec Bruxelles ? Pour en savoir plus, descendez avec nous quelques volées d’escalators, et partons à la découverte des trésors cachés du métro bruxellois. Au programme de la balade, entre autres… – Le « Zigzagramme« , à ne pas « zyeuter » trop longtemps… ; – Le « Passage inconnu« , de François Schuiten ; – Le « Mille-feuille » qui éclairera votre journée à coup sûr ; – « Happy Metro To You« , de Marc Mendelson, qui lance un regard amusant sur notre société ; – …Mais aussi, comme dans toutes les visites de Brussels By Foot, de nombreuses petites histoires et anecdotes! ai.en: At Les Halles de Schaerbeek, Carla Margarita Manrique presents MOLE, a singular performance blending dark humour, personal testimony, and reflections on suicide.
ai.fr: Aux Halles de Schaerbeek, Carla Margarita Manrique présente MOLE, un spectacle singulier mêlant humour noir, témoignage personnel et réflexions sur le suicide.
ai.nl: In Les Halles de Schaerbeek brengt Carla Margarita Manrique MOLE, een eigenzinnige voorstelling die zwarte humor en persoonlijke getuigenissen over zelfmoord combineert.

events.description: A woman in her room. She’s decided to end it all. Her Opinel kitchen knife isn’t sharp enough, the Ikea mirror refuses to break, and the suicide hotline won’t answer. Death isn’t playing along that night. Around this starting point of gross failure, Carla Margarita Manrique builds a show that completely defies classification, simultaneously a lecture and a horror movie, a buffoonish personal testimony and an endoscopic journey. The subject of suicide is broached as a contentious issue that has been theorised on since antiquity, and presented through a deliberately unstable dramaturgy. Reflecting the constant oscillation between life and death experienced by those who contemplate it. A trained Circassian dancer, Carla Margarita Manrique suspends her body from fake intestines, re-enacting the absurd with precision. Her tool: humour. Not to evade, but to heal. “If I don't turn it into a joke, it will destroy me.” A way to stand proud and poised on a razor-thin line. Five solidarity tickets at €5 will be set aside for each performance of performing arts projects (with some exceptions). Please email reservation@halles.be 9€ / 12 € / 14 € / 16 € / 18 € / 20 €

summary.fr: Le point de départ de ce projet est une expérience personnelle, mais pas unique. Le suicide est un sujet que l’humain théorise depuis l’antiquité, soit pour l’exalter soit pour le condamner (surtout pour le condamner).

ai.en: Le 140 hosts MOLE, a performance exploring the complex topic of suicide through humour and distance. The show invites audiences to question their views beyond taboos.
ai.fr: Le 140 accueille MOLE, un spectacle qui aborde la question complexe du suicide à travers l'humour et la distance. Une invitation à questionner nos tabous en toute légèreté.
ai.nl: Le 140 presenteert MOLE, een voorstelling die het complexe onderwerp zelfmoord benadert met humor en afstand. Het stuk nodigt uit om tabogen te doorbreken.

events.description: Peu importent les raisons pour lesquelles quelqu’un·e décide d’en finir avec sa vie, c’est un sujet polémique et une question de débat éthique, religieux, médical, économique, sociologique et politique. Pourtant, personne n’échappe aux réflexions autour de sa propre mort. Avec du recul (et beaucoup de thérapie), une évidence s’impose : aborder un sujet aussi lourd passe par la légèreté et la distance qu’offrent l’humour. Le spectacle propose un cadre où les spectateur·ices sont invité·es à questionner leur rapport au suicide, à réfléchir au-delà des tabous, pour se planter, pour se donner le droit d’être frustré·es, pour rigoler du tragique, peut-être pour essayer de comprendre.

In Tokyo, he recently crossed paths with Japanese double bassist Motoi Kanamori, with whom he immediately felt a strong musical affinity. For their first album together, Ear of the Dragon, they form a quartet with two young talents from the Brussels jazz scene. At the piano, Brussels Jazz Festival 2026 festival artist Wajdi Riahi brings harmonic inventiveness, while Diogo Alexandre drives the music forward with his tight and adventurous drumming. With infectious energy, the quartet delivers resolutely acoustic jazz in which different musical worlds come together. album release: Ear of the Dragon (2026, Hypnote Records)

ai.en: Papa Roach at ING Arena in Brussels on Saturday 28 November 2026, on the Rise of the Roach world tour.

events.description: PAPA ROACH LE SAMEDI 28 NOVEMBRE 2026 À L'ING ARENA, BRUXELLES ! Papa Roach poursuit son impressionnante tournée mondiale Rise Of The Roach, qui a déjà rempli des salles à travers le Royaume-Uni, l'Europe et l'Amérique du Nord. Après son passage très attendu à Werchter Parklife le 28 juin prochain, le groupe californien offrira à ses fans belges une occasion parfaite de le voir en salle avec sa plus grande production jamais réalisée, le samedi 28 novembre 2026 à l'ING Arena de Bruxelles. Une date exceptionnelle qui mettra en lumière toute la puissance et l'intensité d'un groupe dont les prestations live comptent parmi les plus spectaculaires de la scène rock actuelle. Depuis sa formation au milieu des années 90 en Californie autour du charismatique Jacoby Shaddix, Papa Roach n'a cessé de repousser les frontières du rock alternatif. Révélé au grand public grâce à son deuxième album 'Infest' (2000), porté par l'incontournable single "Last Resort", le groupe est rapidement devenu la voix d'une génération. Plus de vingt-cinq ans après la sortie de ce disque fondateur, Papa Roach continue d'écrire son histoire avec la même passion et la même sincérité. Doublement nommé aux Grammy Awards, récompensé par plusieurs disques de platine et fort de onze albums studio, le quatuor s'est imposé comme l'un des piliers du rock moderne. Son catalogue cumule aujourd'hui près de 10 milliards d'écoutes à travers le monde, tandis que ses trois derniers singles, "Even If It Kills Me", "BRAINDEAD"…

ai.en: ILA presents their new album Motherland at Ancienne Belgique, exploring themes of nature and migration. Produced with Mikko Gordon, the record blends personal history with universal stories.
ai.fr: ILA présente son nouvel album Motherland à l'Ancienne Belgique, explorant nature et migration. Réalisé avec Mikko Gordon, le disque tisse des récits personnels et universels.
ai.nl: ILA stelt hun nieuwe album Motherland voor in de Ancienne Belgique over natuur en migratie. De plaat, geproduceerd met Mikko Gordon, verbindt persoonlijke en universele verhalen.

events.description: Deux ans après leur premier album, Ayna, ILA revient avec Motherland, qui révèle un groupe plus ambitieux et plus riche que jamais. Enregistré avec le producteur de renom Mikko Gordon (Idles, The Smile), l'album explore les thèmes de la nature et du père de Cicek, tissant un fil conducteur universel.Motherland est né de l'idée que nous, êtres humains, vivons avec des fragments de nous-mêmes. « Nous laissons tous des traces de nous-mêmes dans des lieux, chez les autres, et même dans nos rêves. Mais nous nous adaptons, nous réinventons nos rêves et apprenons à accepter leur propre évolution », explique chanteuse Ilayda Cicek. « L'histoire a commencé avec mon père, lorsqu'à la fin des années 80, il a pris l'avion pour la Belgique, laissant derrière lui en Turquie tout ce qu'il aimait : sa famille, sa ville, sa langue. Les rêves qu'il a emportés avec lui ont disparu dans la mer ou ont été emportés par le vent. » Mais il a persévéré, appris à vivre avec ce qui avait disparu et comblé le vide par un nouveau départ.La présence de son père se fait sentir dans la seule chanson turque de l'album, Deniz, « la mer » en turc. La chanson est inspirée d'un poème du père de Cicek, où la mer est utilisée comme métaphore de la persévérance et de la force intérieure. « J'ai repris deux ou trois vers et j'ai écrit une chanson autour. C'était incroyable de voir à quel point un texte de mon père s'accordait parfaitement avec l'idée que j'avais déjà pour l'album. La boucle était bouclée. »Une…

events.description: Get ready for an extraordinary musical experience! Arkane, the vocal group that fuses the power of collective singing with the raw energy of rock and hard rock, invites you to an unforgettable concert on 28.11.2026 at the Ancienne Belgique. More than just a concert, Arkane is a shockwave, a cry from the heart, a celebration of music in all its forms. Under the musical direction of Emeline Burnotte, this 150-voice choir reinvents rock and hard rock standards, shattering clichés and revealing all the emotional power of these too-often overlooked genres.Accompanied by a live band made up of Mat Mirol (bass), Emeline Podgornik (drums), Adrien Larock (keyboards), Jean-Bertrand Sellom and Greg Hallet (guitars) and directed by Simon Paco, Arkane's backing singers revisit the great classics and forgotten nuggets of protest music. On the programme: Muse, Imagine Dragons, Nightwish, Shaka Ponk, Placebo, Evanescence, Iron Maiden, U2 and many other surprises...A vibrant, organic and electrifying show that transcends the boundaries of traditional choral singing and takes you on a real musical and human adventure.Accessible to people with reduced mobilityDo you have a question? sftm.site@gmail.com

ai.fr: Le Wild Classical Music Ensemble et Fournèz apportent énergie punk-rock et rythmes maloya au Beursschouwburg. Découvrez une aventure musicale interculturelle.
ai.nl: Het Wild Classical Music Ensemble en Fournèz brengen punk-rockenergie en maloyaritmes naar de Beursschouwburg. Ontdek een intercultureel muzikaal avontuur.

events.description: The Wild Classical Music Ensemble brings together musicians with and without disabilities. Their unique sound is a blend of punk/rock riffs, fanatical rhythms and fiery flute and synth flights, over which gravitate multi-voiced, multi-lingual vocals that scratch harshly as much as they comfort. In 2024 they met musicians from the local music scene in Réunion Island, where music is deeply rooted in Maloya and Sega. The adventure continues with the newly formed group Fournèz, which brings together Gilles Lauret (Danyèl Waro), Baptiste Clément (Mouvman alé), and Benjamin Rebolle (Mouvman alé, Alsimi). This artistic and human journey will culminate in 2026 with an album that builds bridges between cultures and peoples, released via Born Bad and Bongo Joe.The project aims to blend the participants’ diverse relationships with music and language, while snippets of poetry are tenderly exchanged between French and Creole. Singer Françoiz Breut was brought on board to bridge these different linguistic worlds and features on two songs of the album. Vyin mon dalon features Marie Lanfroy from Saodaj and Carlo de Sacco from Grèn sémé.This concert will take place at Beursschouwburg.

events.description: Sounds of the Cities invites you to discover the musical cultures of migrant communities in Antwerp and Brussels from 2026 to 2028. Across a series of six concerts, you will encounter musical traditions from around the world that have become an integral part of the cultural heartbeat of these cities today,. Traditions that continue to evolve, reinvent themselves and connect people across borders and genres. For this second edition, Sounds of the Cities turns its focus to the rich musical traditions of Iran with Aram, a brand-new trio bringing together three exceptional musicians from distinct musical traditions. A shared love of poetry, captivating melodies and subtle percussion lies at the heart of this unique collaboration. Although each musician brings a different musical background, they share an extraordinary sensitivity that makes attentive listening and spontaneous improvisation feel effortless. Shahab Azinmehr is a master of the Persian long-necked lutes tar and setar. Alongside his virtuosic playing, his warm, velvety voice brings a remarkable emotional depth to the music. Turkish kemençe virtuoso Derya Türkan bridges centuries-old Ottoman traditions and the contemporary global music scene with exceptional artistry and expressive power. Percussionist Robbe Kieckens completes the trio with a refined rhythmic language that draws connections between diverse musical cultures, creating a rich and deeply expressive musical dialogue. The Persian word Aram means peace…

events.description: Cinéclube Panorama Brasilis presents a special screening dedicated to Brazilian filmmaker Camila de Moraes, featuring MÃE SOLO (2021, 20 min) and O CASO DO HOMEM ERRADO (2017, 77 min), followed by an online discussion with the director. Born in Rio Grande do Sul, Camila de Moraes is a filmmaker, screenwriter and journalist whose work explores race, gender, memory and social justice. Her films have been widely presented at festivals in Brazil and abroad. MÃE SOLO follows women raising their children alone, exposing the everyday challenges of single motherhood. O CASO DO HOMEM ERRADO revisits the 1987 killing of Júlio César de Melo Pinto, mistaken for a criminal and shot by the Military Police, exposing one of Brazil's most emblematic cases of police violence and structural racism.

events.description: Le duo Oog in Oog, composé du violoniste et joueur de bandolim syrien Shalan Alhamway et de la violoniste baroque néerlandaise Marrie Mooij, interprète des chants traditionnels syriens et ira-kiens, chantés aussi en Palestine, en dialogue avec la musique européenne des XVIIe et XVIIIe siècles. La force universelle et fédératrice de la musique s’en dégage. The Singer of Wind and Rain est un cycle de chansons basé sur cinq poèmes palestiniens mis en musique par le compositeur libano-américain Gregory Youtz. Les poèmes de Salem Jubran, Sulafa Hijawi et Tawfiq Zayyadd s’inscrivent dans la tradition pales-tinienne du SUMUD, cette résistance quotidienne qui consiste à refuser de disparaître et à pré-server une vie normale. Areen Sweetat récite les poèmes en arabe, tandis que le Brussels Brecht-Eislerkoor chante à quatre voix en anglais, accompagné par le paysage sonore de Kobe Baeyens. Une traduction en français et en néerlandais est prévue.

events.description: Dare Balogun is a British-Nigerian DJ, writer, broadcaster and archivist based in London. His practice is committed to traditional African music: vinyl only, research-led, built for the dancefloor, and held together by one connected idea, that the dance forms of West and Central Africa (Highlife, Juju, Soukous, Makossa and Palm wine) are the foundation of modern Black dance music. Most of the practice runs through Roots to Rhythm, the project and living archive he co-founded with Grace Shelley: a monthly residency on NTS Radio and a series of listening sessions and parties. The work has moved between cultural institutions, listening bars, club nights and museums, from the Barbican and Southbank Centre in London to Public Records in New York, PAMM in Miami, Radio Radio in Amsterdam and SAVVY Contemporary in Berlin.﻿

Having been based in Brussels for several years now, the alto saxophonist Federico Milone has been racking up awards, both for his performances and his recordings, a testament to his undeniable talent. A true heir to the purest tradition of his instrument – eloquent and virtuosic – he has developed a modern jazz style rooted in a crystal-clear and exhilarating post-bop sound.With just a few months to go before the release of his fifth album as bandleader, due out next year, he is performing tonight with his regular quartet, accompanied by musicians well versed in the high-flying artistry of his playing. An evening full of energy, just the way we like it.

events.description: On the programme is the Glosa Sinfónica Margariteña, Venezuelan composer Inocente Carreño’s tribute to his homeland. Drawing inspiration from several traditional songs such as Margarita es una Lágrima, the Canto Del Pilón, the Canto de Velorio and Los Tiguitiguitos this impressionist work ranks among the musical masterpieces of Latin America. More than 7,000 kilometres away, the Madrid sun moved Manuel de Falla to compose some of his most fiery pieces, such as the Danza ritual del fuego from his ballet El amor brujo and the Spanish dances from El sombrero de tres picos. Between the two composers, there is but a short step – or rather, La Mer sketched in all its vividness, danger and mystery by Claude Debussy. events.description: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart's Requiem is a masterpiece of mystery, grief, and divine beauty. Written on the edge of mortality, this monumental choral work plunges listeners from the terrifying thunder of the Dies Irae to the heartbreaking, unfinished grace of the Lacrimosa. Under its new Musical Director, Joris Derder, the Brussels Choral Society will take to the Bozar stage for an unforgettable night of timeless sacred music, performing the famous Requiem as well as Josef Rheinberger's hopeful Stabat Mater. Also on the programme: Samuel Barber's serene Adagio for Strings and John Rutter's soothing Musica Dei donum. Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, Requiem KV 626 Josef Rheinberger, Stabat Mater op.138 Samuel Barber, Adagio for Strings John Rutter, Musica Dei donum Liesbeth Devos soprano Ekaterina Romanova alto Timothy Veryser tenor Charles Dekeyser bass La Passione Orchestra The Brussels Choral Society Joris Derder conductor

events.description: The Shit Show is an underground cabaret in Marseille heavily inspired by British punk culture, where anything can happen. Absurdity and even stupidity are embraced there as political tools. And that inevitably leads to colorful performances where “shit” and “show” are constantly intertwined. So how could we not associate them with Anal Pompidou, the Marolles cabaret led by performance artist Simon Van Schuylenberg and his husband Steven Sommereyns? With their “Bottom-up” initiative, specializing in “D.I.Y. trash,” Anal hopes that rents will soon drop in Louise, Dansaert, Petit Sablon, Grand Sablon, in front of the European Parliament, and throughout the municipality of Uccle. Cuddles wraps up with this Franco-Belgian production with its orifices wide open! events.description: “I fall / I fall / I fall to my knees and worship the eternal music.” — Guðrún Eva Mínervudóttir, Ad Genoa Polar landscapes are made of mass and light—of low rumbles, thunderous crashes, and vast silences. In such a place, human beings are only temporary survivors. What stands between us and the infinite? The fragile thread of our voices, trembling as they try to anchor us to eternity. Like water, they can be solid, fluid, or fleeting, as in Hillborg’s Mouyayoum. For Messe des Glaces, Jean-Luc Fafchamps drew inspiration from accounts of polar expeditions. The choir and soprano evoke endless plains of dazzling white, where bears and walruses roam. The trombones, meanwhile, conjure the chaos and infernal groaning of immense masses of ice, drifting apart like crumbling cathedrals. Music may be eternal, but we are not. And neither, for much longer, will be the ice.

events.description: FIRST PART : 14 young virtuosos playing together Ensemble de Guitares du Conservatoire Royal de Bruxelles conducted by Hugues Navez, « Dreams », Vivaldi, Piazzolla, Marquez, Pujol (Belgian premiere)... Inaugurated by Ilse & Nicolas Alfonso in 1965 and one of Europe's oldest, the unique guitar class at the Conservatoire Royal de Bruxelles-École Supérieure des Arts comprises numerous very high standard Belgian and foreign students. Hugues Navez, assisted by Thomas Montagne and Thomas Vanin, has been the full professor of this class since 1999. The Conservatoire offers these future professionals the opportunity to perform regularly on stage : Château du Karreveld, Flagey, the Brussels Parliament, the Brussels Musical Instruments Museum (MIM), the Université Libre de Bruxelles (ULB), Maison de la Musique, the Salon Musicora in Paris... Conducted by their professor, current students perform together and share their passion with the public. SECOND PART : Accordion & guitar, a surprising alchemy - For the first time in Belgium Duo Gorka Hermosa, accordion & Alejandro Ceballos, guitar (Spain) « Ecos de Falla en el Norte » by Falla, Bacarisse, Sáinz de la Maza, Hermosa (Belgian premieres)…

ai.en: Sergi López and Jorge Picó present Non Solum in Spanish at Centre Culturel d'Uccle. This critically acclaimed existential comedy celebrates twenty years on stage.
ai.fr: Sergi López et Jorge Picó présentent Non Solum en espagnol au Centre Culturel d'Uccle. Cette comédie existentielle saluée par la critique célèbre vingt ans de parcours.
ai.nl: Sergi López en Jorge Picó brengen Non Solum in het Spaans in het Centre Culturel d'Uccle. Deze existentialistische komedie viert twintig jaar succes op het toneel.

events.description: LA PIÈCE SERA DONNÉE EN ESPAGNOL. LE MÊME SPECTACLE SERA DONNÉ EN FRANÇAIS LE 27 NOVEMBRE AU CENTRE CULTUREL D'UCCLE. Empieza una comedia existencial. Un hombre llega empujando una puerta que alguien ha dejado abierta y parece que todo va bien hasta que la presencia sospechosa de un segundo personaje rompe la intimidad inicial. No pasa mucho tiempo hasta que un tercer hombre aparece para descubrir que los tres son iguales. Desesperado, este hombre multiplicado se transforma en muchos otros para responder a una pregunta: ¿qué está pasando aquí? Y mientras nosotros reímos, alguno de estos hombres no entiende nada y se quiere ir. Otro canta una canción. Otro nos explica que teme volverse loco mientras el resto se enfada cuando se dan cuenta de que, en realidad, todos son el mismo. Juntos viajan hacia el paraíso, donde parece que ser igual y diferente es lo mismo, donde todas las preguntas pueden tener respuesta. En su trayecto les acompaña algún bolero, una caja de madera y unas gafas de plástico que parecen falsas. Su destino es dudar relativamente de absolutamente de todo. ¿Qué pasa? ¿No me creen? Non Solum celebra 20 años de trayectoria consolidada, avalada por crítica y público. Con una solvencia teatral más que contrastada, esta pieza escrita por Sergi López y Jorge Picó se ha convertido en un referente escénico, tanto por su profundidad como por su originalidad. Su protagonista, Sergi López —en plena actualidad mediática gracias a su papel en Sirat, galardonada con el…

events.description: You were taught to stay quiet. To soften your words. To hide your accent. To lower your volume until you became easier to accept. We refuse. Every language. Every laugh. events.description: The exhibition pays tribute to a transversal approach to architecture: it foregrounds a practice that hybridises the expertise of architects, landscape architects and urban planners with the civic engagement of associations, activists and citizens. Right to the city brings together "militant archives" (Isabelle Doucet), the Archives d'architecture moderne (AAM) and the Sint-Lukasarchief – both rooted in the late 1960s and integral to Kanal Architecture’s DNA – alongside contemporary initiatives such as Filter Café Filtré’s Open Streets and the decolonial projects of the Laboratory of Mixed Realities. Brussels has a particular and often traumatic relationship with modernity and modernisation – commonly and mockingly referred to as "Brusselisation". This "peacetime demolition" has left deep scars on the urban fabric, most notably through the transformation of the Quartier Nord, located directly next to Kanal, via the Manhattan plan. Right to the city situates itself within this history, linking the memory of surrounding neighbourhoods to urgent contemporary issues – the climate crisis, circularity, gender and postcolonialism. The exhibition and its accompanying programme follow a dual logic. On the one hand, they position Kanal Architecture as a new forum for spatial debate, bringing together experts and residents. On the other hand, they affirm the institution’s DNA as a site of cross-disciplinary practice that focuses on architecture, landscape and urban ecosystems. Right to…

events.description: En Avant ! revient à Flagey et sur la Place Sainte-Croix, à Ixelles ! C'est quoi encore En Avant ! ? En Avant ! C'est une fête qui informe sur les droits de l'enfant et les font vivre. C'est organisé par la Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles dans le cadre de la Journée internationale des droits de l'enfant. Et on y fera quoi ? Comme d'habitude, on vous a concocté une programmation pour tout les goûts et pour tous les âges de 0 à 18 ans : des ateliers créatifs, des jeux, des spectacles. On fera de la musique, on dansera, on créera des pochettes et des mégaphones, on écoutera des histoires, on s'initiera au handisport, on jouera avec des robots et, puis, on parlera des droits de l'enfant et des jeunes... Bientôt, le programme complet sur le site officiel de la fête Et ça coûte cher ? Non, c'est GRATUIT ! C'est pas chouette, ça ? Il faut réserver ? Non, réserve juste ta journée ou quelques heures dans ton agenda ou celui de tes parents pour profiter de la fête. Et tu viens quand tu veux ! Et tout le monde est le bienvenu ! En plus, cette année, on s'est associé aux rencontres Jeu t'aime, qui invitent parents et enfants à jouer. En Avant ! est une initiative de la Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles, coordonnée par Badje et la Coordination des ONG pour les droits de l'enfant, avec le support logistique de Yellow Events et les soutiens de la Cocof et la Commune d'Ixelles.

events.description: Chaque stage sera l’occasion d’explorer une nouvelle facette du Flamenc’O’riental, tout en gardant une place importante au plaisir de danser et à l’échange. Nous terminerons cette série 2026 par une chorégraphie Yallah Olé !! 18 octobre – 10h30 à 13h30 Stage découverte — À la rencontre du Flamenc’O’riental Et si le Flamenco rencontrait la danse Orientale ? Venez découvrir le Flamenc’O’riental, une rencontre entre deux univers dansés aux caractères bien différents, mais qui peuvent se compléter et se répondre. Lors de ce premier stage, nous partirons à la découverte des mouvements fondamentaux du Flamenco et de la danse Orientale, de leurs postures, de leurs bras, de leurs accents et de leurs différentes qualités de mouvement. À travers des exercices simples et accessibles, nous explorerons progressivement la manière de faire dialoguer ces deux langages corporels, avant de les réunir à travers de petits enchaînements. Certains mouvements et enchaînements explorés lors de ce stage pourront ensuite être repris et développés dans les prochains rendez-vous de la série. Ce stage est ouvert aux personnes souhaitant découvrir cet univers, mais également aux danseuses et danseurs ayant déjà une expérience du Flamenco, de la danse Orientale ou d’autres disciplines. Une petite pause gourmande est prévue au cours de la matinée : un moment pour souffler, grignoter, échanger et partager autour de cette première découverte. • 2 novembre – 10h30 à 13h30 Technique & Combinaisons Après la…

ai.en: "Le quartier Stalingrad-Lemonnier: liquidation totale?", a talk on a neighbourhood squeezed by the inner ring road.

events.description: Le quartier Stalingrad-Lemonnier est pris en étau entre la petite ceinture, la jonction ferroviaire Nord-Midi et le centre-ville historique. Ce quartier du Pentagone est le berceau d’une activité commerciale pérenne depuis le 19e siècle. Maintes fois secoué par des grands travaux d’urbanisme au 20e siècle, le quartier, récemment rénové par les pouvoirs publics, est aujourd’hui de nouveau confronté à de très lourds travaux d’infrastructure : la construction du métro Nord, lancée en 2020 par la Région bruxelloise et la STIB. Ce dernier bouleversement pourrait bien menacer l’existence même des commerces autour de l’avenue de Stalingrad. Plus récemment, la décision de la Région de démolir le Palais du Midi pour faire passer son métro a fait l’actualité. L’ARAU avait introduit en 2023 une demande de classement du bâtiment pour préserver ce joyaux architectural, que le gouvernement a décidé de ne pas suivre. Une pétition a été lancée en juin 2026, et les alternatives continuent de mobiliser tout le milieu associatif actif sur le sujet !

title.en: In the Footsteps of Karl Marx
title.fr: Sur les Traces de Karl Marx
title.nl: In de Sporen van Karl Marx

summary.fr: Entre 1845 et 1848, la famille Marx séjourne à Bruxelles. Pendant son séjour, Karl Marx écrit, en compagnie Friedrich Engels, plusieurs livres, dont le Manifeste du Parti Communiste. Ce dernier est devenu la base du socialisme mondial…

ai.en: Walk through central Brussels to discover the places where Karl Marx lived and wrote the Communist Manifesto during his exile. This guided tour explores the young industrial Belgium of the mid-nineteenth century.
ai.fr: Partez pour une promenade guidée dans le centre de Bruxelles sur les traces de Karl Marx et de son séjour en Belgique. Découvrez les lieux historiques où il a vécu et écrit le Manifeste du Parti Communiste.
ai.nl: Wandel door het centrum van Brussel langs de plekken waar Karl Marx verbleef en het Communistisch Manifest schreef. Deze geleide wandeling dompelt je onder in het negentiende-eeuwse industriële België.

events.description: Cette promenade nous conduit à travers le centre de Bruxelles le long des rues et des places où Marx a séjourné et travaillé. Cette balade est aussi une immersion dans la toute jeune Belgique, tout juste indépendante. À cette époque de capitalisme décomplexé, ce tout petit pays était la deuxième puissance industrielle du monde ! QU’ALLEZ-VOUS DÉCOUVRIR ? Indésirable en Allemagne et en France en raison de ses idées, Karl Marx s’exile à Bruxelles en 1845, alors terre d’asile pour les révolutionnaires. La Belgique lui offre un titre de séjour « à la conditon qu’il ne publie pas sur la situation politique actuelle ». Marx, accompagné de son ami Engels, y écrira néanmoins une des oeuvres phares de sa vie de philosophe : Le Manifeste du Parti Communiste ! Le bouillonnement de la ville, son terreau révolutionnaire, mais aussi le tournant capitaliste que prend la société feront du séjour belge de Marx un tournant dans sa pensée et dans son travail. Cette promenade nous conduit à travers le centre de Bruxelles le long des rues et des places où Marx a séjourné et travaillé. Au programme de la balade, entre autres : – Les Galeries Saint Hubert au milieu du 19ème siècle – Son séjour près de la cathédrale Sainte Gudule – Place Royale: son contact avec les révolutionnaires de la révolution Belge – Les discussion qu’il menait sur un appartement au Grand Sablon – Son arrestation et expulsion à la prison Amigo Balade à disponibilité réduite. Le guide qui vous accompagne, jeune retraité et…

summary.en: Mozart meets Beethoven
summary.fr: Mozart meets Beethoven
summary.nl: Mozart meets Beethoven

ai.en: Experience classical masterworks by Mozart, Beethoven, and Berlioz at Bozar. Conductor Michael Schønwandt and violinist Carolin Widmann lead the Belgian National Orchestra.
ai.fr: Découvrez des chefs-d'œuvre classiques de Mozart, Beethoven et Berlioz à Bozar. Le chef Michael Schønwandt et la violoniste Carolin Widmann dirigent l'Orchestre National de Belgique.
ai.nl: Beleef klassiekemeesterwerken van Mozart, Beethoven en Berlioz in Bozar. Dirigent Michael Schønwandt en violiste Carolin Widmann leiden het Nationaal Orkest van België.

events.description: Mozart thinks freely, Berlioz thinks theatrically, Beethoven thinks radically. They listened differently, thought further, and rewrote the rules of their time. In his Fifth Violin Concerto, Mozart lets freedom be heard. The violin sounds neither solemn nor formal, but dreamy and bold, as if the music were inventing itself in the moment. Beauty here is not decoration, but imagination in motion - full of humour, surprise and outward-looking curiosity, crowned by the famous "Turkish" episode. With Beethoven, that freedom becomes a necessity. Two uncompromising chords in the Eroica force the door open to something entirely new. This is no longer music for salons or courts, but a personal statement, driven by tension, conflict, momentum and ambition. Romanticism begins here not as a style, but as an attitude. And then there is Hector Berlioz, the visionary who understood that music could also be theatre and colour. In Béatrice et Bénédict, his urge to let the orchestra speak through untamed contrasts and emotions is already fully present. Led by Michael Schønwandt and featuring internationally acclaimed violinist Carolin Widmann, this concert pays tribute to composers who did not follow their time, but led the way.Enhance your experience beyond the concert with an introduction! The introduction starts at 2 pm and is free upon presentation of your concert ticket.Thanks to the players of the National Lottery and to the Tax Shelter of the Federal Government of Belgium through Gallop…

events.description: gross gross?!what does that mean, gross?when is something gross?life, yes …life itself is simply gross!right?In times of aroma diffusers, anti-lice shampoo, moisturisers, care robots and toilet drain cleaner, it seems like certain things that are part of life are increasingly supposed to be hidden, disguised, concealed. Just not today. Most likely, the stage’s cleaning crew happens to be sick today. Take a look at the things grown-ups have learned to look away from and discover what happens when this life steps out of the shadows and into the stage lights.With titillating images, live music and minimal language, you’ll balance on an edge where belly laughs, a bit of disgust, and a tiny bit of aversion for dead things quickly transform into beauty, fascination and a lust for life.Warning: This fun, somewhat absurd and burlesque performance for anyone from 4 years old may give adults slight feelings of discomfort.

events.description: Festival Osmose: Violin Concert Julien Poli began playing the violin at the age of nine at the Conservatoire National de Région in Bayonne. By the age of eleven, he was already performing as a soloist with the conservatory's youth orchestra in Vivaldi's The Four Seasons. Four years later, he was awarded a first prize in violin, followed the next year by an advanced performance prize. A series of concerts followed, in which he performed Bach's violin concertos and Brandenburg Concertos as a soloist. His studies later took him to the Paris Conservatoire, where he studied with Maryvonne Le Dizès (Paganini Competition first prize winner and concertmaster of the Ensemble intercontemporain) and obtained his diploma in musical studies. In 2007, he joined the Royal Conservatory of Brussels, studying violin and viola at master's level in Marc Kowalski's class. He later completed his teaching diploma at the Royal Conservatory of Liège in the class of Philippe Koch. Julien has received guidance from renowned musicians including Roland Daugareil, Gérard Poulet, Jean-Jacques Kantorov, Christophe Poiget, Véronique Bogaerts, Dimitri Ivanov and Ralph Gothoni, as well as the Artis, Prazak and Danel Quartets. He has also received scholarships from Horlait-Dapsens, the Lions Club and Raynaud-Zurfluh. He regularly performs with the Brussels Philharmonic, the orchestra of La Monnaie, the Luxembourg Philharmonic Orchestra, the Royal Opera of Liège and Opera Ballet Vlaanderen, and has performed…

events.description: Our artistic director makes no secret of the fact that he is a huge fan of Bill Evans. One of the most influential pianists in the history of jazz and a key architect of the global and timeless success of *Kind of Blue*, the Plainfield native enjoyed a career spanning more than 30 years, with a style that was unique and instantly recognisable from the very first note. A magician of harmony, a master of romanticism and the inventor of interplay with his legendary trio alongside Scott LaFaro and Paul Motian, he was a prolific composer and a ‘reinventor of standards’ who changed forever the way those who followed him would play the piano. Joachim Caffonnette, who has studied the American pianist for many years, immersing himself in his style, will attempt to do him justice this Sunday afternoon.

events.description: Entre spectacle et atelier, place à l’expérience ! À la lisière de la lumière, nous vous invitons à plonger dans une expérience intérieure, à suivre le fil d’Ariane dans le labyrinthe de vos ressentis. Des propositions guidées vous accompagneront pour explorer cet espace intime, en confiance. Au fond, la pratique somatique, c’est simple : respirer amplement, regarder tendrement, se détendre délicatement. C’est aussi prendre le temps d’habiter son corps, d’écouter ce qui s’y joue et de reconnaître ce qu’il a à nous dire, dans un monde qui ne nous laisse pas toujours cet espace. La performance se tissera comme une toile, entre danses à regarder et mouvements à explorer soi-même, ponctuée de citations de philosophes, d’écrivain·es, de scientifiques et d’artistes de notre temps. Autant de voix et de pensées pour nourrir nos réflexions, faire résonner nos expériences et ouvrir des espaces de rencontre. Peut-être qu’au fil des mouvements et des mots, une résonance commune se dessinera : une autre manière d’habiter nos corps, de prendre place et d’imaginer ensemble ce que nous voulons en faire. Spectateur·ice ou participant·e ? Et si vous pouviez être les deux ? Compagnie de danse amateur inspirée notamment par la Skinner Releasing Technique et la composition instantanée, Zodiac Dance partage une danse accessible et joyeuse, notamment auprès de publics fragilisés. Avec ce premier Spectatelier, elle propose une autre manière de vivre la danse : sortir de sa place habituelle de…
